default.notes: A visitor visa must be obtained in advance from a Dominica high commission, embassy or honorary consulate. Dominica waives visas for around a hundred nationalities, so check the current exempt list before assuming you need one.

groups.notes: CARICOM nationals move freely within the community — visitors are normally granted a six-month stay on arrival, and skilled nationals with a CARICOM certificate may live and work.

No visa is needed, but The Bahamas and Haiti take part in CARICOM's free-movement arrangements only partially — the automatic six-month community stay is not guaranteed, so confirm the length of stay you will be given before booking.

No visa needed. Immigration officers often stamp a short initial stay — commonly around 21 days — based on your ticket and accommodation; the Immigration Division in Roseau can extend it to a maximum of six months. Ask for the time you need at the desk.
Chinese citizens enter without a visa under the bilateral waiver agreement, commonly for up to 30 days — confirm the current allowance before booking.
Russian citizens are covered by a bilateral visa-waiver agreement, usually reported as up to 90 days — confirm with a Dominica mission before travelling.

DM.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Dominican citizens.

IN.notes: Indian passport holders are not clearly listed as visa-exempt — plan on applying for a visitor visa in advance. Some sources report a Commonwealth short-stay waiver, so confirm with a Dominica mission before booking.
